newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal raises petrol, diesel prices - NOC official.
newsitem.headline: Nepal raises petrol, diesel prices - NOC official.

text.p: Nepal on Friday raised the domestic price of petrol by 14.7 percent and that of diesel by 25 percent, a senior official of the state-owned Nepal Oil Corporation (NOC) said.
NOC general manager Ramagya Chaturvedi told Reuters the price rises, which took effect on Friday, followed increases in the prices of petroleum products in the international market.
NOC has a monopoly over the import and distribution of petroleum products in the Himalayan kingdom, and imports some 600,000 tonnes of petroleum products every year.
Petrol will now sell for 39 rupees (68 U.S. cents) a litre, up from 34 rupees, while diesel will cost 17.50 rupees, up from 14 rupees.
The price of kerosene was raised 15.7 percent to 9.50 rupees a litre, the NOC official said.
Chaturvedi said cooking gas would now sell for 25,195.90 rupees a tonne, an increase of 53 percent.
Petroleum products last year accounted for 6.1 percent of the total energy consumption in the Himalayan kingdom, one of the world's 10 poorest nations. Kerosene and diesel are subsidised in Nepal.
Officials said NOC had been losing about 30 million rupees a month since last October because of the subsidies.
"With the latest increase, we will not be incurring any loss now," Chaturvedi told Reuters. ($1 = 57.1 rupees)
